relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with a clinical/flow-cytometric diagnosis of LAD-I and no genetic testing: "the patient was diagnosed as having a mild variant of LAD-1".
method_note: Case report, read by hand; one small Python script in scratch assembled the JSON and the 20-row checklists. In scope: the patient (diagnosis of LAD-I by clinical features and flow cytometry; no ITGB2 sequencing or variant is reported, so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported is null) and his three deceased sibs, described as affected ('three sib deaths ... all because of severe gastroenteritis with similar recurrent skin infections'); sib sex not stated, so labels 'sibling of patient', 'sibling of patient 2', 'sibling of patient 3' in order of the ages listed (one year, two years, five months). The parents and three living sibs ('totally free') were neither tested nor affected and get no rows. Sib features come from one statement naming the group of three sibs (evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'); consanguinity for sibs taken from the shared parents. Age at diagnosis taken as the age at presentation (6 years) since the diagnosis followed that evaluation; age at last evaluation left not reported because psoriasis developed later ('One year ago') with no age given. Vital status of the patient not stated explicitly, left not reported. ESR 35 mm/hr and CRP 96 mg/dL were not labelled abnormal by the authors and were not recorded as features. 'Otherwise, he was clinically free' excludes nothing specific. Weight/height at 50th percentile recorded as excluded short stature/low weight; checklist 'failure to thrive' left not reported (current percentile does not address growth history). Ulcerated skin swellings were not described as necrotic, so the 'necrotic skin ulcers' checklist item is not reported. Sib 'gastroenteritis' was not mapped to the 'gastrointestinal infections' checklist item (infectious cause not stated). Psoriasis not mapped to 'autoimmune complications' (authors do not call it autoimmune). The authors' speculation about 'allelic heterogeneity' and dysfunctional CD18 is not a reported variant. No contradictions found.
